2-3: Keep hair, shoes, and overall appearance neat and professional. Uniform works with presentation — both signal care for learners and families.
Every campus follows the same uniform schedule so parents see one Silverleaf standard, not local dress habits.
If a uniform is lost or damaged, report it through your campus process instead of substituting random clothing.
2-4: School fees and activity payments must go through official channels. Staff are never a cash collection desk.
Do not hold pocket money or fundraising cash for students. Redirect to the approved process.
If a payment conversation happens, keep it professional and point people to finance or the posted payment instructions.
2-5: After emergency first aid, document what happened and report to a senior staff member who informs parents or caregivers.
Encourage open communication. Secrets between adults and children are a safeguarding red flag.
In your first weeks, learn the named safeguarding contacts on your campus and how to escalate after hours if needed.
2-6: Personal device use must not put school data at risk. Prefer school systems for learner and parent information.
Tools like Canva, PowerSchool, and ClassDojo are school resources — use them professionally and keep logins private.
Tech maintenance keeps classrooms running. Report broken devices early instead of working around unsafe setups.
2-7: Contractors and volunteers handling Silverleaf data must follow the same confidentiality rules as employees.
Do not keep personal files forever on your laptop. Follow retention guidance and delete securely when no longer needed.
Families trust us with sensitive information. Careless sharing damages that trust and can harm children.
2-8: Do not involve yourself in toileting or feeding beyond what is strictly necessary for the child's age and development.
Never condone or participate in behaviour that is illegal, abusive, or unsafe around children.
If a child is in immediate danger, take urgent protective steps and alert senior staff without delay.
2-18: Never post confidential Silverleaf, learner, or staff information on social media, even in private groups.
During placements, supervised learning may require access — that does not mean you may share freely outside supervision.
Signing the agreement means you understand these duties and accept the consequences of breach.
2-1: If any handbook rule is unclear, ask your manager or H R early — do not invent an answer in front of families.
Your everyday conduct shapes Silverleaf's reputation with parents and the wider community.
2-2: Health, safety, and employee wellbeing are part of H R policy, including responsible workplace approaches to sensitive health matters.
The manual can be reviewed and amended. Stay alert when H R communicates updates.
